newsitem.title: USA: Canada LPG slightly down, liftings light.
newsitem.headline: Canada LPG slightly down, liftings light.

text.p: Canada liquefied petroleum gases (LPG) were slightly lower this week amid warm weather and light liftings on the pipelines, players said Thursday.
Weak U.S. markets also pressured Canadian markets lower, particularly in western Canada which tracks off the Midcontinent.

Spot propane in the western hub of Edmonton fell about 0.75 cent since last Thursday to 35.00 cents and 35.25 cents a gallon. Players said the product may further weaken to within the traditional 5.00 cent spread with Conway, Kansas.
Eastern hub spot propane in Sarnia also dipped about a half cent to 41.00/42.00 cents in the midst of warm weather.
Cold weather expected next week is not likely to bump up the market significantly due to recent light liftings that have left many players well stocked.
"The market seems pretty stable so I don't forsee a huge increase or decrease next week," said one Sarnia trader.
Meanwhile, Sarnia butane got some play as refiners returned to the table to top up on supply before the reid vapor pressure in gasoline is reduced.
Sarnia butane traded 43.00/43.25 cents. --((Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1631))
